card.name: Sentence-opening What before a clause
card.fires_on: The word "What" (or "what") starting a sentence or clause in essays and opinion web text, especially as a free relative like "What she ordered" or a rhetorical "Yet what of...". Weaker on some determiners such as "these", "very" or "human" before a noun.

modes.label: Sentence-initial What
modes.description: Capitalized "What" opens a sentence after a period, introducing a clause or question.
modes.example: << What>> we can learn from, however, is

modes.label: Mid-sentence what
modes.description: Lowercase "what" after "Yet" or "that" introduces a clause or a rhetorical question.
modes.example: Yet<< what>> of women? Did they not keep the

modes.label: Determiners before a noun
modes.description: Occasional modifier words like "these" or "very" or "human" just before a noun phrase.

card.plain: It lights up on the word "What" when it starts a sentence or clause in essays, as in "What she ordered...".
